current_bottleneck: 460a shows that a full-covariance Gaussian day-vector transition density is too broad and too weakly conditional: it overcovers, under-learns cross-cell correlation and mean reversion, and worsens level/distributional fidelity.
last_result_summary: 460a implemented a deployable empirical-normal-score day-vector Gaussian density p(delta S_t | history, S_<t), trained by exact NLL and sampled ancestrally. It scored 2/11, failing surface, coverage, conditionality, time_series, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, cross_cell_correlation, mean_reversion, and pathwise_jump_realism.
next_step_recommendation: Do a post-experiment mechanism read before the next experiment: preserve the explicit likelihood paradigm, but reject the independent day-Gaussian transition as the next core unless its learned covariance/correlation and path width failure can be fixed without calibration knobs.
